subject: pharmacology
title: Fludrocortisone, Potency, HPA Suppression, Cushingoid Features and Steroid Withdrawal

steps.tx: **Fludrocortisone** is the mineralocorticoid specialist: fluorination multiplies aldosterone like activity (sodium retention, potassium and hydrogen excretion, volume expansion) to roughly 125 times hydrocortisone with useful glucocorticoid spill, dosed in micrograms (50 to 300) for adrenal insufficiency's salt half and off label for orthostatic hypotension. Its surrogates are lying and standing pressure, potassium and renin; overdose is hypertension, oedema and hypokalaemia wearing an endocrine costume.
steps.say: Fludrocortisone is bottled aldosterone in microgram doses; pressure, potassium and renin steer it.

steps.tx: **Glucocorticoid potency** tables compare anti inflammatory power per milligram (hydrocortisone 1, prednisolone 4, methylprednisolone 5, triamcinolone 5, dexamethasone 25 to 30) against duration (short, intermediate, long) and mineralocorticoid residue, and fluency in the three columns converts any steroid question into arithmetic. Potency is not efficacy: a potent drug at an equivalent dose does not outperform, it merely lasts longer and suppresses the axis deeper per course.
steps.say: Potency converts doses, duration converts risk; neither converts a weak indication into a strong one.

steps.tx: **HPA axis suppression** follows dose and duration arithmetic: courses under two to three weeks at modest doses rarely suppress meaningfully, while prednisolone above 7.5 mg daily (or equivalents) beyond three weeks should be assumed suppressive, with recovery taking weeks to a year after long therapy. Evening dosing, long acting agents and divided doses suppress most. Testing (morning cortisol, Synacthen stimulation) and endocrine liaison govern withdrawal after serious exposure.
steps.say: Three weeks above seven point five milligrams: assume suppression and plan the exit like a landing, not a jump.

steps.tx: **Cushingoid features** catalogue chronic glucocorticoid excess on the body the drug was mimicking: central obesity with moon face and buffalo hump, purple striae, proximal myopathy, hypertension, hyperglycaemia, osteoporosis, skin thinning and bruising, cataracts, mood and psychosis, growth suppression in children and infection masked until advanced. The catalogue is a monitoring checklist at every chronic review, each item triggering dose reduction pressure or organ protection in parallel.
steps.say: Read the Cushingoid catalogue as a checklist at every review; each feature found argues the dose down.

left.title: Visible Cushingoid signs
points: Central weight, moon face, supraclavicular pads
Purple striae, thin skin, easy bruising
Proximal weakness on chair rise testing

steps.tx: **Cushingoid features** record what chronic glucocorticoid excess does to the body the drug is copying: central obesity, moon face, buffalo hump, purple striae, and proximal myopathy, together with hypertension, hyperglycaemia, osteoporosis, thin bruising skin, cataracts, mood change or psychosis, growth failure in children, and infection that stays quiet until late. At each review the list is a checklist. Every item found pushes the dose down or adds protection for the organ already harmed.
steps.say: Chronic steroid excess produces central fat, a moon face, a buffalo hump, purple striae, and weak shoulder and hip muscles, plus high blood pressure, high glucose, thin bones, easy bruising, cataracts, mood change, slowed growth, and hidden infection. Each finding at review is a reason to lower the dose or protect the organ involved.

steps.tx: **Steroid withdrawal** separates three syndromes students conflate: true adrenal insufficiency on cessation (axis suppressed, crisis risk), steroid withdrawal syndrome (lethargy, myalgia, mood fall with a recovered axis and miserable physiology), and disease relapse misread as withdrawal. Tapering treats the first and prevents confusion with the third: reduce swiftly to physiological range while disease allows, then crawl (1 mg prednisolone per month territory), switch to hydrocortisone for the final approach, and test the axis before declaring independence.
steps.say: Crisis, withdrawal misery and relapse are three different patients; taper speed and axis testing separate them.

left.title: Withdrawal syndromes
points: Withdrawal syndrome: aches, lethargy, low mood, axis intact
Each has a different next move

right.title: Taper architecture
points: Fast to physiological range if disease permits

Sick day rules continue until axis proven

steps.tx: **Steroid induced hyperglycaemia follows** hepatic glucose output and insulin resistance with a postprandial accent, worst on morning intermediate acting doses by afternoon and evening, screened by capillary profiles rather than fasting alone and treated often with basal or mixed insulin scaled to the steroid curve, then de escalated in lockstep with the taper lest the steroid fall strand the patient hypoglycaemic on yesterday's insulin.
steps.say: Steroid glucose peaks after lunch and falls with the taper; insulin must dance the same choreography backwards.

nodes.label: Insulin matched to the steroid curve

steps.tx: **Bone protection is protocol**, not virtue: calcium and vitamin D repletion, bisphosphonate therapy by fracture risk tools in adults on three months plus of prednisolone at 7.5 mg equivalents and above (lower thresholds with prior fractures or high risk), densitometry baselines and falls review. Children trade growth plates into the bargain, making paediatric chronic steroids a growth chart surveillance contract with endocrine partnership.
steps.say: Three months of steroids earns a bone plan the same week, not after the first fracture.

left.title: Bone protection bundle
points: Fracture risk assessed and bisphosphonate by threshold

right.title: Growth surveillance in children
points: Height velocity charted at every visit
Lowest dose and alternate day strategies

steps.tx: **Infection under steroids hides** and multiplies: fever and inflammatory markers blunt while tuberculosis reactivates, fungi and Pneumocystis colonise at sustained higher doses (prophylaxis thresholds near prednisolone 20 mg for a month with other risks), varicella can kill the non immune, and live vaccines wait. Screening (TB, hepatitis B, strongyloides where endemic) precedes long high dose courses and biologics combined with them, an order of operations examinations increasingly test.
steps.say: Screen before you suppress: TB, hepatitis B and threadworm where relevant, and prophylax at sustained high doses.
